lines: P-csrf-stable (DEC-70; finding-63, review-43 F2, finding-62 item 3): two commits on track/p-csrf-stable, not pushed, rebased or landed: acf2dcd 'fix(auth): keep one CSRF token per web session across reads' and ed8d674 'fix(auth): harden the stable CSRF read and normalise rotation ids' (security review of acf2dcd, verdict fix). Backend only; frontend untouched, 89b2ffc recovery kept.

WHY READS ROTATED: BE-022 (90352c7, its log BE-022-web-csrf-recovery.md) overwrote the token on every read assuming only a tab that lost it reads; no review or security note asked for it. Kept: per-session token (session id in the HMAC), new token on every refresh rotation with the old refused, channel predicate, Origin/Sec-Fetch check, bytesEqual compares.

HOW (acf2dcd): sign-in CSRF = deriveCsrfToken(refreshKey, sessionId, 0, 'sign-in'), session id chosen with randomUUID before the insert (createWebSession takes sessionId). A read derives the token for (generation, last_rotation_id or 'sign-in') and returns it with no write when it matches; otherwise it rotates once to the derived token (sessions from v0.18.0 or earlier, a read by an older backend after rollback, a REFRESH_HMAC_KEY change). The grace replay (previous refresh, same rotationId, 30 s) accepts the previous CSRF or the replayed rotation's token, nothing older.

FOLLOW-UP (ed8d674): F2 every admin read in the tests asserts user.userId and roles (onboarding), and a client web test asserts the client userId and two stable reads; F3 webRefresh lower-cases rotationId before derivation, storage and the grace compare (Zod uuid() accepts upper case; the uuid column stores lower case, so a read replaced the token); F1 a read that finds the session by refresh cookie answers 401 SESSION_INVALID, no revoke, unless the cookie is current (unused, unrevoked) or the session's immediately previous one within the grace; F6 comments at webAuth.ts header and rotateWebCsrf corrected, plus the grace-branch comment ('previous or replayed CSRF'); no new comments.
Accepted trade-off (in the ed8d674 body): within 30 s, the previous refresh cookie plus the rotationId refresh without the previous CSRF token.

F1 effect: after the grace, a tab still holding the previous cookie gets 401 from the read and signs out without revoking the family; before, the read succeeded and the refresh then revoked it. Lost-reply retry within the grace still keeps the session (test 3 green). The access-cookie path is unchanged.

UNCHANGED (rule 11): routes, cookie names, headers, response shapes, error codes (SESSION_INVALID and AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED already answered by the read), contracts, no migration. Native bearer untouched (nativeAuth.ts not edited; its rotationId compare is still case-sensitive, see LEFT).

COMPAT v0.18.0 frontend -> this backend: reads no longer change its token; another tab's restore no longer refuses its writes; lost-reply retry keeps the session; crypto.randomUUID sends lower case so F3 changes nothing for it. This frontend -> v0.18.0/v0.17.0 backend: reads rotate again, 89b2ffc recovery re-reads once and resends with the same Idempotency-Key, F2 window as in v0.18.0. Deploy: one repair rotation per existing session, other open tabs see one CSRF_INVALID on the next write (recovered by this frontend).

TESTS (backend_controller/test/integration/authWeb.integration.test.ts, 15): two reads return the sign-in token + write after the second; after a refresh old token 403 CSRF_INVALID, new 200; lost reply retried within the grace keeps the session, older token 401 revokes; client read names the client and keeps its token; upper-case rotationId: read keeps the rotated token and the retry replays it; used refresh cookie: the older one 401 SESSION_INVALID, the previous one within grace 200, the previous one at +31 s 401, session still usable; another session's token 403.

RUNTIME STEPS (UNVERIFIED, not run): (a) admin web, tab 1 signed in with a form open, open tab 2; submit in tab 1: no 403, no recovery GET /v1/auth/web/csrf for the write; both tabs' csrf reads return the same token and user. Same on the client web app (/v1/auth/client/web/csrf). (b) access cookie expired (10 min), two tabs: tab 1 request refreshes; tab 2 then reads tab 1's rotated token and refreshes again; still signed in. LEFT / DOUBTFUL: two tabs refreshing in the same round trip with different rotationIds still revoke the family (pre-existing; a frontend cross-tab refresh lock, e.g. Web Locks, would serialize them). Native refresh still compares rotationId case-sensitively (nativeAuth.ts, out of lane: native untouched); released apps send lower case. plans/admin-improvements.md line 1261 and finding-63 still describe read rotation; finding-62 item 3 answered (TESTED); DEC-70 can move to built when landed.

P-csrf-stable (DEC-70; finding-63, review-43 F2, finding-62 item 3): built on track/p-csrf-stable, one commit acf2dcd 'fix(auth): keep one CSRF token per web session across reads'. Not pushed, rebased or landed. Backend only; frontend untouched (89b2ffc recovery kept as is).

WHY READS ROTATED (git log -S rotateWebCsrf/webRecoverCsrf, blame): BE-022 (90352c7, 2026-07-21, its log BE-022-web-csrf-recovery.md) overwrote the token on every read with 'no grace: the client had already lost it', i.e. it assumed only a tab that lost its token reads. No review or security note asked for rotation on read; Completed/.../LOGS/risk_and_decision.md (~1339-1360) and TASK/021 record multi-tab CSRF_INVALID as an accepted consequence and the mixed-pair edge as deferred.

WHAT THAT PROTECTED AND HOW IT IS KEPT: a token is per session and per channel and changes with the refresh chain. Still so: the sign-in token is new per session (session id is in the HMAC), every refresh rotation issues a new token and the old one is refused, rotateWebCsrf keeps its channel predicate, reads still need the Origin/Sec-Fetch check and that session's own cookies, compares stay bytesEqual (timingSafeEqual).

HOW (webAuth.ts): sign-in CSRF = deriveCsrfToken(refreshKey, sessionId, 0, 'sign-in'); the session id is chosen with randomUUID before the insert (createWebSession now takes sessionId). Rotation tokens were already derived(sid, gen, rotationId). A read derives the token for (generation, last_rotation_id or 'sign-in'), returns it and writes nothing when the stored hash matches.

Read repair: when the stored hash differs (session signed in on v0.18.0 or earlier with a random token, a read by an earlier backend after a rollback, or a REFRESH_HMAC_KEY change) the read rotates once to the derived token via rotateWebCsrf; later reads are stable. Gen 0 cannot collide with a rotation token (rotations are gen >= 1, rotationId must be a uuid).

Reads still answer 401 AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED / SESSION_INVALID and 403 ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE as before (code paths unchanged). csrfTokenExpiresAt is still now+10 min. csrf_expires_at/last_seen_at were written by every read but are read nowhere in src; a stable read no longer touches them.

GRACE (finding-62 item 3), read: both runtimes (v0.18.0 and HEAD) keep rotationId until a refresh succeeds and read CSRF before each refresh. Old backend (STATIC): lost reply -> read rotates to a random token -> retry with previous refresh + random token fails the previous-CSRF check -> family revoked (refresh_reuse). Stable read alone still revoked (it returns the rotation's token; RC-C proves it). Fix: the grace replay (previous refresh cookie, same rotationId, within 30 s) accepts the previous CSRF or the token of the rotation it replays, nothing older; it reproduces the same pair with no write.

UNCHANGED (rule 11): routes, cookies and names, headers, request/response shapes, error codes, contracts, no migration. Native bearer channels untouched (nativeAuth.ts, createBearerSession, rotateRefresh not edited).

COMPAT v0.18.0 frontend -> this backend: it reads before each refresh and has no automatic re-read on a refused write; reads no longer change its token, so another tab's restore no longer breaks its writes; its token now changes only on a refresh rotation (as before). Lost-reply retry keeps the session.

COMPAT this frontend -> v0.18.0/v0.17.0 backend (rollback): reads rotate again; the 89b2ffc recovery re-reads once, checks the user and resends with the same Idempotency-Key; the F2 window returns as in v0.18.0. A derived sign-in token issued here is validated by hash on the old backend like any token. Roll forward again: one repair rotation per session.

DEPLOY IMPACT: once per existing web session, the first read after deploy rotates the token (repair). Other open tabs of that session see one CSRF_INVALID on their next write: this release's frontend recovers and resends once; a v0.18.0 tab shows Not confirmed until it refreshes or reloads (what any second tab caused before).

TESTS (backend_controller/test/integration/authWeb.integration.test.ts, replacing the test that asserted rotation on read): (1) two reads return the sign-in token, logout with it after the second read 200; (2) after a refresh the read returns the rotated token, old token 403 CSRF_INVALID, new 200; (3) refresh reply lost, refresh-cookie-only read returns the lost rotation's token, retry with it 200 reproducing the same refresh cookie and token, retry with the tab's previous token 200, retry with the older sign-in token 401 and the session is revoked; (4) another session's token 403 CSRF_INVALID on a write, own token 200.

RED CONTROLS (each restored from a saved copy, cmp identical, tree clean after): bc3d2d1f RC-A read rotates again (old webRecoverCsrf body): 4 failed/8 passed (tests 1-4); fadda155 RC-B sign-in token random again: 2 failed/10 (tests 1, 4); 5b001c50 RC-C grace accepts only the previous CSRF: 1 failed/11 (test 3, retry got 401); aee1bd22 RC-D sign-in token derived without the session id: 1 failed/11 (test 4).

GREEN on acf2dcd, clean tree, Node 24 container: 52ffecc2 contracts npm ci && build; 69d35e5d backend npm ci && check (102 files/1209 tests, coverage 81.68/84.93/86.66/81.68, both smokes); 2792cf4f backend test:integration --coverage.enabled=false (75 files/599 tests). Frontend not touched, so no frontend checks run.

RUNTIME STEPS (UNVERIFIED, not run): (a) admin web, sign in in tab 1, open a form; open tab 2 (its restore reads CSRF); submit in tab 1: no 403 and no second GET /v1/auth/web/csrf for the write in the network log; GET /v1/auth/web/csrf in both tabs returns the same csrfToken. Same for the client web app (/v1/auth/client/web/csrf).

RUNTIME STEPS (b): let the access cookie expire (10 min) with two tabs open; trigger a request in tab 1 (csrf read + refresh 200), then in tab 2: tab 2's read returns tab 1's rotated token, its refresh rotates again, session stays signed in. (c) optional: block the refresh response once (devtools) and retry within 30 s: the session survives.

LEFT / DOUBTFUL: two tabs refreshing in the same instant with different rotationIds still revoke the family (pre-existing, not a read issue: the second carries either the used refresh cookie with another rotationId or the new cookie with the pre-rotation token, the mixed-pair edge still deferred in webAuth.ts). A cross-tab refresh lock on the frontend (Web Locks) would serialize them; with stable reads the second tab would then read the post-rotation token. Step (b) shows it only if both tabs refresh in the same round trip.

LEFT: a CSRF read accepts a used refresh cookie of an active session (lockByRefreshTokenHash ignores used_at), pre-existing; it returned a fresh token before and returns the current one now, same exposure. The grace replay now needs {old refresh cookie, rotationId} rather than also the pre-rotation token, but anyone holding the cookie and rotationId runs in the tab and holds that token too.
